title: Treat unparseable YAML lines as unresolved, not silently-dropped
context: The scanner silently ignored any line it couldn't parse (quoted keys, merge keys, etc.), which is dangerous: a dropped constraint makes a selector/labels map MORE permissive, risking false-positive edges between non-matching resources.
decision: Generalized the existing `blockTemplated` mechanism (renamed `unresolvedContainers`) to mark ANY container with an unparseable line as unresolved, not just those with explicit `{{ }}` template injections. 'I can't tell' now reads as 'unresolved,' the same as a real template.
consequences: Eliminates a class of false positives where dropped quoted/merge keys silently made selectors over-match
Subsumes multiple error cases (quoted keys, merge keys, etc.) under one conservative principle
Allows removal of the parallel `pendingBlockKey` mechanism, which mutation testing showed was fully redundant with BARE_TEMPLATE_LINE handling
alternatives_rejected: Continue silently ignoring unparseable lines (prior behavior) — treats 'can't parse' as 'absent,' unsafe for permissive containers
Add a strict parsing mode that errors on unknown shapes — would stop the whole scan, less resilient to real-world YAML variation
